summary: Frontend-only Playwright verification of WhatsApp Phase 2. All requested flows PASS: login as demo@test.com -> nav-whatsapp -> /whatsapp route -> EmptyState 'Belum ada akun WhatsApp' (when accounts empty) -> click wa-add-account opens scrollable qr-modal (class includes both overflow-y-auto + max-h-[90vh]) -> qr-image rendered in ~2.3s (<<6s) -> qr-modal-close works -> account card persists with 'Scan QR'/'Connecting' badge -> clicking card shows 'Pilih chat untuk baca pesan' right-panel placeholder. Composer test-ids (wa-attach-btn, wa-file-input, wa-message-input, wa-send-btn) verified present in WhatsApp.jsx source via grep (lines 572, 565, 585, 592) — not testable at runtime without an active connected session. Cleanup via DELETE /api/whatsapp/accounts/{sid} returns API list to []. Backend 17/17 pytest already verified by main agent; not re-run here.

integration_issues.issue: After DELETE all accounts via API returns GET=[] (verified), reloading /whatsapp re-shows an account card (e.g. 'TEST_resume') instead of EmptyState. Backend appears to auto-resume/restore a persisted Baileys session on page load, re-creating an account row. Not blocking, but cleanup is not idempotent from the UI perspective. Consider clearing Baileys auth_info files when DELETE /api/whatsapp/accounts/{sid} is called, or excluding restored sessions until user opts in.

action_items: Investigate auto-resume behavior: after DELETE returns 200 and GET returns [], a subsequent page reload re-introduces an account (label 'TEST_resume'). DELETE handler may need to also remove Baileys session files / disable auto-restore for deleted SIDs to keep cleanup deterministic.
(No other actions needed) iteration_5 LOW polish item is already fixed — qr-modal now has max-h-[90vh] + overflow-y-auto.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still large (~5000 lines). Splitting into routers (whatsapp/, prospects/, auth/, templates/) is still recommended per file-size guideline (>700 lines).
WhatsApp.jsx polls /chats every 8s and /messages every 5s plus /status every 2s — three concurrent intervals per active page; consider SSE or WebSocket pushed from backend to reduce load and latency.

DELETE /api/whatsapp/accounts/{sid} appears to not fully purge the underlying Baileys session, allowing UI to re-show the account on reload. Either purge session files on delete, or filter resumed sessions that no longer have a DB row.

success_rate.backend: 100% (17/17 pytest from prior run, not re-executed)

test_credentials: Owner: demo@test.com / demo1234 (verified working). Login response uses key 'token' in localStorage.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed. Test created 2 transient WA accounts (Baileys sessions returning QR within ~2.3s), then cleaned both via DELETE /api/whatsapp/accounts/{sid}. Final GET /api/whatsapp/accounts -> [] confirmed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 frontend WhatsApp flow is solid. Composer-level UI (wa-attach-btn / wa-file-input / wa-message-input / wa-send-btn at /app/frontend/src/pages/WhatsApp.jsx lines 565-592) can only be tested with a connected Baileys session (real phone scan) — skip in automated tests. Auto-accept window.confirm before clicking delete buttons. Toast 'Welcome back' can briefly overlap top-right action buttons; either wait ~3s or remove via JS before clicking wa-add-account. The DELETE -> reload -> account reappears behavior is a backend auto-resume side effect — flag it to main agent rather than treat as test flake.

rca_of_the_issue: Reload-after-cleanup repopulating an account: DELETE removes the DB row but Baileys auth_info on disk persists; on app/page refresh the backend auto-loads any on-disk sessions and re-creates account rows. Mitigation: in DELETE handler, also rm -rf the Baileys auth_info directory for that session_id, or maintain a 'deleted' tombstone that auto-resume must consult before recreating.
